# vti-01 Raman stacking read — result (2026-08-24)

Device: vti-01, 3LGr (trilayer per owner's characterization), dual-gated
hBN-encapsulated Hall bar. Data: WITec project `vti-01.wip`, sample
`73474_`, four maps + three video frames, all 2026-05-28 UTC (see
`provenance.md`).

## Headline

**The mapped graphene sheet is a mixed-stacking crystal: interleaved ABA
and ABC lamellar domains at roughly 50:50 by area, at 5–20 µm domain
scale.** A pickup event recorded *inside the file* (between video 002 →
video 004, i.e. ~20:10–20:19 UTC) removed most of the sheet between map
003 and map 005. The portion that was picked up — the likely device
graphene if vti-01 was built from this pickup — is therefore covered only
by pre-pickup map 003 and is **mixed-domain, not single-stacking**. The
remnant left on the substrate (the "tombstone", fully mapped post-pickup)
is ABC-dominant (~78%). The two fine maps (006, 008) contain no Raman
signal (stale 1064 nm laser selection) and are uninformative.

No build-stage testimony was supplied; the pre-/post-pickup staging above
is in-file evidence (timestamped videos + maps), and nothing in the inputs
says which portion (picked-up sheet vs remnant) became the vti-01 channel.

## 1. Per-region verdicts

Stage frame = WITec stage µm coordinates as stored in-file (scan-axis
rotation ~0.5° included via per-pixel coordinates). Raster masks with the
same label numbers: `regions.npz` / `regions.png` (layers `labels_pre` =
map-003 state, `labels_post` = map-005 state).

| Region | Centroid (x, y µm) | Stage stamp | Verdict (strength) |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 sheet, ABC domains (label 1) | (−12050.1, 1282.8); lamellae across x −12078…−12028, y 1265…1303; 528 µm² | pre-pickup (map 003, 19:57 UTC) | **ABC** (strong) |
| R2 sheet, ABA domains (label 2) | (−12054.8, 1287.3); interleaved with R1; 516 µm² | pre-pickup (map 003) | **ABA** (strong) |
| R1+R2 sheet as a whole (the picked-up material, minus remnants) | x −12078…−12027, y 1264…1304 | pre-pickup (map 003) | **mixed ABA/ABC, ~50:50, lamellar 5–20 µm domains** (strong) |
| R5 tombstone remnant, interior (label 5) | (−12040.6, 1278.9); x −12047…−12035, y 1266…1295; 236 µm² | post-pickup (maps 005 @20:20; corroborated by 003 pre-pickup) | **ABC** (strong) |
| R6 tombstone remnant, W edge strip + SE patch (label 6) | (−12042.4, 1282.1); mostly x −12047…−12044 column and (−12038, 1268) patch; 66 µm² | post-pickup (map 005) | **ABA** (weak — edge-adjacent, 66 px) |
| R3 thick wedge (label 3) | (−12073.5, 1292.5); 66 µm² | present pre & post | multilayer graphene >3L, Bernal-consistent 2D (consistent-with); not the trilayer |
| R4 graphite sliver/chunk (label 4) | (−12068.6, 1265.1); 39 µm² | present pre & post | graphite, decisive; not device-relevant |
| Strip right of remnant | x −12035.5…−12031, y 1267…1290 | post-pickup | **uninformative** (optically dark, no G band, Si slightly enhanced ×1.04, broad ~1350 hump — likely pickup-tear debris/residue; not graphene, no sharp hBN 1366 line) |
| Map 006 footprint | center (−12037.6, 1294.5), 28×13 µm | post-pickup, 20:27 | **uninformative** — detector noise only (recorded 1064.4 nm excitation; no signal on Si CCD) |
| Map 008 footprint | center (−12037.5, 1269.9), 18×8 µm | post-pickup, 20:30 | **uninformative** — detector noise only (same cause) |

## 2. Evidence

All spectra: 532.338 nm excitation, axis −890…+3617 rel. cm⁻¹; per-pixel
despiked, linear-baselined; scripts `s0`–`s11` regenerate everything.

**Thickness uniformity (the domain split is not a layer-count step):**
- G-band area is single-moded across the sheet: ABC domains 4492, ABA
  domains 4551 (median CCD·cm⁻¹; 1.3% apart). Si 520 attenuation identical:
  0.821 vs 0.821–0.840 of bare-substrate value. A 3L↔4L step would move G
  by ~25–30%. (`final_stats.txt`, `histograms.png`)
- 2D/G area ratio 2.26, D/G ≈ 0.0005 (pristine). 2D FWHM 60–63 cm⁻¹ —
  few-layer, consistent with 3L; layer number is not independently
  verifiable from these data (named hedge #2).

**Stacking discrimination — four independent signatures, all pointing the
same way** (cluster medians; k-means K=2 on area-normalized 2D lineshapes,
1344 sheet pixels from maps 003+005; `final_lineshapes.png`,
`final_stats.txt`):

| Metric | ABC-like cluster | ABA-like cluster | expected ABC−ABA sign (lit.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2D single-Lorentzian center | 2695.0 cm⁻¹ | 2697.4 cm⁻¹ | red-shifted ✓ |
| 2D single-Lorentzian FWHM | 63.4 cm⁻¹ | 60.3 cm⁻¹ | broader ✓ |
| 2D lineshape | sharper peak at ~2683 cm⁻¹, enhanced 2630–2690 weight, kink near 2710 | rounder maximum at ~2690–2697 | more asymmetric ✓ |
| G center | 1579.9 cm⁻¹ | 1581.1 cm⁻¹ | red-shifted ~1 cm⁻¹ ✓ |

- 3-Lorentzian decomposition of cluster means (center/FWHM/amp):
  ABC-like: (2641.5, 31, 0.0009), (2683.2, 36, 0.0116), (2711.3, 41, 0.0095);
  ABA-like: (2643.1, 45, 0.0005), (2686.5, 39, 0.0112), (2712.9, 41, 0.0094).
  The discriminating weight sits in the sharper, red-shifted main component
  and the low-ω shoulder (difference curve peaks at ~2678 cm⁻¹,
  `final_lineshapes.png` right panel).
- Not an instrumental artifact: Rayleigh (−0.5 cm⁻¹) and Si (519.50 cm⁻¹)
  anchors are identical in maps 003 and 005 (`calib_check.txt`); both
  clusters are populated within each map.
- Not strain/doping gradients: domains are lamellar with sharp (1–2 px =
  1–2 µm) boundaries interleaved across a contiguous uniform-thickness
  crystal (`regions.png`, `clusters_k3.png`) — the canonical ABA/ABC domain
  morphology — rather than smooth radial gradients.
- Cross-map consistency through the pickup: the tombstone footprint reads
  72% ABC-like in pre-pickup map 003 and 78% in post-pickup map 005 — two
  independent acquisitions agreeing on the same physical region.

**The pickup event (staging evidence):** video 002 (19:55) shows one large
dark sheet covering the whole survey footprint, matching map 003's G-area
region shape in the stage frame (`video_002.png` vs `compare_worldframe.png`);
videos 004/007 (20:19/20:29) show only the tombstone + wedge remnants.
Map 003's G-region does not match video 004 but matches video 002;
map 005 registers on video 004 at r = 0.77 (`orient_results.txt`,
`orient_overlay.png`). Raster orientation was verified against the video
(no flip; `s6_orient.py`).

**Region classes:** wedge: G area 7443 (1.6× sheet), Si 12899 (more
attenuated), 2D 2699.8/58.4 — thicker Bernal-like multilayer. Graphite
sliver: Si ~500 (blocked), 2D peak 2712 with 2690 shoulder — classic
graphite doublet (also validates the lineshape method).

## 3. Confidence and named hedges

Overall: **the mixed-domain read of the sheet and the ABC-dominant read of
the remnant are strong**; no single-region call is offered as decisive.

1. **ABA/ABC assignment direction rests on literature signatures recalled
   from memory** (2D red-shift + broadening + asymmetry and G red-shift for
   ABC at 2.33 eV — Lui et al. / Cong et al. 2011). The *existence* of two
   equal-thickness stacking domains is data-decisive; the *labeling* of
   which is which would invert if those signatures were misremembered. Four
   concordant signatures make inversion unlikely.
2. **Layer count is the owner's testimony.** These data show a uniform
   few-layer sheet (2D FWHM ~60–63, complex multi-component; 2D/G 2.26)
   consistent with 3L, but no independent layer-count map exists. If it
   were 4L, the Bernal-vs-rhombohedral split would still stand as read.
3. **Which region is the device channel is not determined by the inputs.**
   No frame bridge (GDS/optical of the finished device) and no build-stage
   testimony were supplied. In-file evidence shows most of the sheet was
   picked up on 2026-05-28 20:10–20:19 UTC; if the device came from that
   pickup, the channel is somewhere in the mixed R1/R2 mosaic and the
   channel-scale stacking depends on where the Hall bar landed within it.
   If the device was made later from the remnant, R5/R6 applies
   (ABC-dominant with ABA edge strips).
4. **Post-map history unknown.** The maps predate the cooldown by ≥3
   months (map 2026-05-28, read 2026-08-24); stacking domains in trilayers
   are mobile under processing (encapsulation, annealing, gating can move
   ABA/ABC walls). The read is a statement about 2026-05-28, not about the
   cooled device.
5. **R6 (remnant ABA strips) is edge-adjacent** (one ~2 µm column plus a
   small patch, 66 px); edge-mixed spectra could mimic the ABA direction.
   Hence "weak".
6. **Maps 006/008 carry no information** — their "1064.4 nm" laser
   selection produced no CCD signal; the intended fine maps of the remnant
   never happened (see provenance, excitation-tag anomaly).
7. Minor: 003↔005 registration agrees to ~1 µm but the G-threshold edge
   sits ~1 px differently between maps; domain-boundary positions carry
   ±1–2 µm uncertainty.

## 4. What would firm it

- **A reference spectrum from a known-stacking flake on the same tool**
  (or published 532 nm ABA/ABC trilayer lineshapes) to lock the assignment
  direction of hedge #1 without memory reliance.
- **A frame bridge**: optical image or GDS of the finished vti-01 Hall bar
  registered to this stage frame (or to the picked-up flake on its stamp),

- **Build-stage testimony**: whether the device came from the 20:10 pickup

# Device card — vti-01 (trilayer graphene)

*Session device card for vti-01 on the **VTI** cryostat. Deployed into the
measurement directory alongside the working notebooks. This card carries
**physical truth**: what is wired, the hardware, the outer safety box,
the provided gate operating limits, and the provided contact
configuration. The CNP location and (n, D) calibration are established
in-session (see the session brief).*

## Identity
- **Device id**: `vti-01`
- **Material**: trilayer graphene (`3LGr`).
- **Owner**: Jordan
- **Fridge**: VTI (variable-temperature insert). Base (sample)
  temperature ≈ 1.2–1.3 K.
- **Status**: cold, wired — hardwired breakout, no contact mux; no CNP
  location on record.

## Gate stack
- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by a Keithley 2400**
  (`k_2400_tg`) — sweeps use `k_tg.volt` (5 mV step pacing; the measure
  notebook's setup cells bind `k_tg`).
- **Back gate** (`k_bg`): graphite on hBN, driven by the second
  **Keithley 2400** (`k_2400_bg`).
- **Si global back gate** (`k_si`): doped-Si gate through **SiO₂**,
  driven by the **SRS DC205** — bound directly to the driver's ramped
  parameter **`dc205.smart_voltage`** (set ramps at `ramp_rate = 0.5`
  V/s, get reads back `VOLT?`; data column **`dc205_smart_voltage`**).
  The DC205 has **no current readback** — gate-leakage monitoring lives
  on the Keithley `curr` channels (TG/BG) only. `ramp_voltage` steps
  span/50: a full ±50 V traverse moves in ~1 V steps, paced by
  `ramp_rate`. The graphite back gate screens Si from the channel — Si
  couples only to the contacts (contact-doping gate). Operating limit
  provided (below).
- **Gate-stack geometry** (fabrication facts; **geometry prior only** —
  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via
  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`):
  ```python
  from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages
  c_tg = stack_capacitance([(14.9, 3)])           # 14.9 nm hBN
  c_bg = stack_capacitance([(21.4, 3), (0, 3.9)])   # 21.4 nm hBN, no SiO2 term
  ```
  Treat anything derived from these (lever arms, n/D scales, CNP-line
  slope) as uncalibrated until the session's own gate map confirms it.

## Gate operating limits — gate B contract

Gate operating limits for the session:

| Parameter | Operating limit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `k_tg.volt` | **[−0.8, +0.8] V** | provided; geometry ceiling is the hard fence behind it |
| `k_bg.volt` | **[−5.0, +5.0] V** | provided |
| `dc205.smart_voltage` / `dc205.voltage` (Si) | **[−20, +20] V** | provided; DC205 must be on its ±100 V range (RNGE 2) |
| **B field (session cap)** | **\|B\| ≤ 10.0 T** | committed on the `magnet.field` validator (SAFETIES); driver `max_field_T = 14.0` T is the hard backstop |
| **T setpoint (session cap)** | **`set_both` target ≤ 100 K** | provided; committed as a SAFETIES setpoint typo-guard cap. `ratio = 0.95` per the rig card — deviations consent-gated |

- **Gates**: top via **k_2400_tg** (GPIB0::1), back via **k_2400_bg**
  (GPIB0::24), hardwired to their sources.

  range), hardwired to its source.
- **AC excitation / lock-ins**: SR830 family (`sr0` GPIB0::22, `sr1` GPIB0::14, `sr2` GPIB0::19, `sr3` GPIB0::18).

"""f1_extract_videos.py — pull the three stage-registered video images
(the only frame bridge) out of vti-01.wip, with their stage transforms.

Output: fusion_videos.npz with, per video NNN:
  imgNNN (H,W float grayscale), plus worldorigin/scale/rotation arrays,
and a cross-check table printed against raman-provenance.md.
"""
import numpy as np

import f0_parse_wip as f

buf, roots = f.load()
data_node = [n for n in roots[0]["children"] if n["name"] == "Data"][0]


def get(node, path):
    cur = [node]
    for p in path.split("/"):
        cur = [k for c in cur for k in c["children"] if k["name"] == p]
    return cur


by_id = {}
for ch in data_node["children"]:
    if ch["dtype"] != 0:
        continue
    idn = get(ch, "TData/ID")
    if idn:
        by_id[int(f.data(buf, idn[0])[0])] = ch

out = {}
for ch in data_node["children"]:
    if not get(ch, "TDBitmap"):
        continue
    cap = f.data(buf, get(ch, "TData/Caption")[0])[0]
    tag = cap.split("--")[-1]  # e.g. 002
    sx = int(f.data(buf, get(ch, "TDBitmap/SizeX")[0])[0])
    sy = int(f.data(buf, get(ch, "TDBitmap/SizeY")[0])[0])
    raw = f.data(buf, get(ch, "TDBitmap/BitmapData/Data")[0])
    px = np.frombuffer(raw, dtype="<u4").reshape(sy, sx)
    # 4 bytes/px: try BGRA split; grayscale video -> channels equal
    b = (px & 0xFF).astype(np.float32)
    g = ((px >> 8) & 0xFF).astype(np.float32)
    r = ((px >> 16) & 0xFF).astype(np.float32)
    gray = (r + g + b) / 3.0
    stid = int(f.data(buf, get(ch, "TDBitmap/SpaceTransformationID")[0])[0])
    st = by_id[stid]
    wo = f.data(buf, get(st, "TDSpaceTransformation/ViewPort3D/WorldOrigin")[0])
    sc = f.data(buf, get(st, "TDSpaceTransformation/ViewPort3D/Scale")[0]).reshape(3, 3)
    rot = f.data(buf, get(st, "TDSpaceTransformation/ViewPort3D/Rotation")[0]).reshape(3, 3)
    utc = f.data(buf, get(ch, "TData/CreationOrChangeUTCTime")[0])[0]
    ang = np.degrees(np.arctan2(rot[1, 0], rot[0, 0]))
    print(f"{cap}: {sx}x{sy}px, {sc[0,0]:.5f} um/px, TL world=({wo[0]:.2f},{wo[1]:.2f}), "
          f"rot={ang:+.3f} deg, chan-equal={np.allclose(r,g) and np.allclose(g,b)}, {utc}")
    out[f"img{tag}"] = gray.astype(np.float32)
    out[f"wo{tag}"] = wo
    out[f"scale{tag}"] = sc
    out[f"rot{tag}"] = rot
    out[f"utc{tag}"] = np.array(utc)

np.savez_compressed("fusion_videos.npz", **out)
print("saved fusion_videos.npz:", sorted(out))

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of — build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong — check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** — every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

"""f2_registration.py — the registration artifact for the vti-01 fusion.

One stage-µm frame carrying everything that CAN be registered:
  panel A: video 002 (pre-pickup) + map-003 region labels (labels_pre)
  panel B: video 004 (post-pickup) + map-005 region labels (labels_post)
  panel C: the transport channels — topology-only device schematic,
           explicitly NOT registered (no stage↔device bridge in inputs).

Outputs: registration.png, registration.json.
Also prints a quantitative orientation/overlay check (video gray sampled
at region world-coords: sheet must be darker than background).
"""
import json

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
from matplotlib.transforms import Affine2D

V = np.load("fusion_videos.npz")
R = np.load("inputs/regions.npz", allow_pickle=True)
x_um, y_um = R["x_um"], R["y_um"]

# identity hues (validated): ABC blue, ABA orange; context in neutrals
C_ABC, C_ABA = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834"
GRAY_EDGE, GRAY_WEDGE, GRAY_GRAPHITE = "#b8b6ae", "#8a887f", "#55534c"
INK, INK2 = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e"
SURF = "#fcfcfb"

LABEL_COLOR = {1: C_ABC, 2: C_ABA, 3: GRAY_WEDGE, 4: GRAY_GRAPHITE,
               5: C_ABC, 6: C_ABA, 7: GRAY_EDGE}


def world_transform(tag):
    """pixel (col,row) -> stage µm, from the in-file WITec transform."""
    wo, sc, rot = V[f"wo{tag}"], V[f"scale{tag}"], V[f"rot{tag}"]
    M = rot[:2, :2] @ sc[:2, :2]
    return np.array([[M[0, 0], M[0, 1], wo[0]],
                     [M[1, 0], M[1, 1], wo[1]],
                     [0, 0, 1]])


def sample_video_at(tag, xw, yw):
    """video gray at world points (bilinear-free nearest lookup)."""
    A = np.linalg.inv(world_transform(tag))
    img = V[f"img{tag}"]
    p = A @ np.vstack([xw, yw, np.ones_like(xw)])
    c, r = np.round(p[0]).astype(int), np.round(p[1]).astype(int)
    ok = (c >= 0) & (c < img.shape[1]) & (r >= 0) & (r < img.shape[0])
    out = np.full(xw.shape, np.nan)
    out[ok] = img[r[ok], c[ok]]
    return out


# ---- quantitative overlay check: sheet pixels must be darker than bg ----
XX, YY = np.meshgrid(x_um, y_um)
for tag, lay in (("002", "labels_pre"), ("004", "labels_post")):
    L = R[lay]
    sheet = np.isin(L, [1, 2, 5, 6])
    bg = L == 0
    gs = sample_video_at(tag, XX[sheet], YY[sheet])
    gb = sample_video_at(tag, XX[bg], YY[bg])
    print(f"video {tag} vs {lay}: gray sheet {np.nanmean(gs):.1f} "
          f"vs background {np.nanmean(gb):.1f} (sheet darker => aligned)")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- figure
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16.5, 6.2), facecolor=SURF)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.05, right=0.985, top=0.86, bottom=0.16, wspace=0.18)

XLIM = (-12085, -12018)
YLIM = (1258, 1310)

def draw_panel(ax, tag, lay, title):
    img = V[f"img{tag}"]
    tr = Affine2D(world_transform(tag)) + ax.transData
    ax.imshow(img, cmap="gray", origin="upper",
              extent=(0, img.shape[1], img.shape[0], 0),
              transform=tr, interpolation="bilinear",
              vmin=np.percentile(img, 1), vmax=np.percentile(img, 99))
    L = R[lay]
    rgba = np.zeros(L.shape + (4,))
    for k, col in LABEL_COLOR.items():
        m = L == k
        rgba[m] = matplotlib.colors.to_rgba(col, alpha=0.5)
    ax.imshow(rgba, origin="lower", interpolation="nearest",
              extent=(x_um[0] - .25, x_um[-1] + .25, y_um[0] - .25, y_um[-1] + .25))
    ax.set_xlim(*XLIM); ax.set_ylim(*YLIM)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_title(title, color=INK, fontsize=11, loc="left")
    ax.set_xlabel("stage x (µm)", color=INK2, fontsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(colors=INK2, labelsize=8)
    for s in ax.spines.values():
        s.set_color("#d8d6cf")
    # 10 µm scale bar
    ax.plot([-12082, -12072], [1260.5, 1260.5], color=INK, lw=2)
    ax.text(-12077, 1262, "10 µm", color=INK, fontsize=8, ha="center")

draw_panel(axes[0], "002", "labels_pre",
           "A  PRE-pickup — video 002 (19:55 UTC) + map-003 regions")
axes[0].set_ylabel("stage y (µm)", color=INK2, fontsize=9)
axes[0].annotate("wedge >3L", xy=(-12073.5, 1292.5), xytext=(-12083, 1302),

axes[0].annotate("graphite", xy=(-12068.6, 1265.1), xytext=(-12062, 1260.5),

                 arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=INK2, lw=0.8))

draw_panel(axes[1], "004", "labels_post",
           "B  POST-pickup — video 004 (20:19 UTC) + map-005 regions")
axes[1].annotate("tombstone remnant\n(78% ABC)", xy=(-12040.6, 1278.9),

                 arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=INK2, lw=0.8))
axes[1].annotate("sheet here was PICKED UP\n~20:10–20:19 UTC\n(mixed ABA/ABC mosaic)",
                 xy=(-12065, 1290), color=INK2, fontsize=8, ha="center")

# ---- panel C: device frame, topology only, explicitly unregistered ----
ax = axes[2]
ax.set_facecolor(SURF)
ax.set_xlim(0, 10); ax.set_ylim(0, 10)
ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
for s in ax.spines.values():
    s.set_color("#d8d6cf"); s.set_linestyle("--")
ax.set_title("C  DEVICE FRAME — NOT REGISTERED to A/B", color=INK,
             fontsize=11, loc="left")

VERDICT = {"sr1": (C_ABA, 1.0, "sr1  B_SD–L4   ABA (strong, two-branch)"),
           "sr3": (C_ABA, 0.45, "sr3  L3–L2      ABA (consistent-with)"),
           "sr2": (GRAY_EDGE, 1.0, "sr2  L4–L1      uninformative")}

    ax.text(xoff, (y0 + y1) / 2 + (0.35 if ch == "sr2" else 0), " " + ch,
            color=INK, fontsize=8, va="center")
for i, ch in enumerate(("sr1", "sr3", "sr2")):
    col, al, txt = VERDICT[ch]
    ax.plot(0.6, 0.9 - 0, marker="none")
    ax.plot([0.5, 0.9], [1.15 - 0.38 * i] * 2, color=col, alpha=al, lw=5)
    ax.text(1.05, 1.15 - 0.38 * i, txt, color=INK, fontsize=8, va="center")
ax.text(5.0, 9.35, "No frame bridge in the inputs links this Hall bar to the\n"
        "stage frame of panels A/B — no optical image of the finished\n"
        "device, no GDS, no build-step testimony. Even whether the\n"

One stage-µm frame carrying everything that CAN be registered:
  panel A: video 002 (pre-pickup) + map-003 region labels (labels_pre)
  panel B: video 004 (post-pickup) + map-005 region labels (labels_post)
  panel C: the transport channels — topology-only device schematic,
           explicitly NOT registered (no stage↔device bridge in inputs).

Outputs: registration.png, registration.json.
Also prints a quantitative orientation/overlay check (video gray sampled
at region world-coords: sheet must be darker than background).
"""
import json

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
from matplotlib.transforms import Affine2D

V = np.load("fusion_videos.npz")
R = np.load("inputs/regions.npz", allow_pickle=True)
x_um, y_um = R["x_um"], R["y_um"]

# identity hues (validated): ABC blue, ABA orange; context in neutrals
C_ABC, C_ABA = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834"
GRAY_EDGE, GRAY_WEDGE, GRAY_GRAPHITE = "#b8b6ae", "#8a887f", "#55534c"
INK, INK2 = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e"
SURF = "#fcfcfb"

LABEL_COLOR = {1: C_ABC, 2: C_ABA, 3: GRAY_WEDGE, 4: GRAY_GRAPHITE,
               5: C_ABC, 6: C_ABA, 7: GRAY_EDGE}


def world_transform(tag):
    """pixel (col,row) -> stage µm, from the in-file WITec transform."""
    wo, sc, rot = V[f"wo{tag}"], V[f"scale{tag}"], V[f"rot{tag}"]
    M = rot[:2, :2] @ sc[:2, :2]
    return np.array([[M[0, 0], M[0, 1], wo[0]],
                     [M[1, 0], M[1, 1], wo[1]],
                     [0, 0, 1]])


def sample_video_at(tag, xw, yw):
    """video gray at world points (bilinear-free nearest lookup)."""
    A = np.linalg.inv(world_transform(tag))
    img = V[f"img{tag}"]
    p = A @ np.vstack([xw, yw, np.ones_like(xw)])
    c, r = np.round(p[0]).astype(int), np.round(p[1]).astype(int)
    ok = (c >= 0) & (c < img.shape[1]) & (r >= 0) & (r < img.shape[0])
    out = np.full(xw.shape, np.nan)
    out[ok] = img[r[ok], c[ok]]
    return out


# ---- quantitative overlay check: sheet pixels must be darker than bg ----
XX, YY = np.meshgrid(x_um, y_um)
for tag, lay in (("002", "labels_pre"), ("004", "labels_post")):
    L = R[lay]
    sheet = np.isin(L, [1, 2, 5, 6])
    bg = L == 0
    gs = sample_video_at(tag, XX[sheet], YY[sheet])
    gb = sample_video_at(tag, XX[bg], YY[bg])
    print(f"video {tag} vs {lay}: gray sheet {np.nanmean(gs):.1f} "
          f"vs background {np.nanmean(gb):.1f} (sheet darker => aligned)")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- figure
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16.5, 6.2), facecolor=SURF)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.05, right=0.985, top=0.86, bottom=0.16, wspace=0.18)

XLIM = (-12085, -12018)
YLIM = (1258, 1310)

def draw_panel(ax, tag, lay, title):
    img = V[f"img{tag}"]
    tr = Affine2D(world_transform(tag)) + ax.transData
    ax.imshow(img, cmap="gray", origin="upper",
              extent=(0, img.shape[1], img.shape[0], 0),
              transform=tr, interpolation="bilinear",
              vmin=np.percentile(img, 1), vmax=np.percentile(img, 99))
    L = R[lay]
    rgba = np.zeros(L.shape + (4,))
    for k, col in LABEL_COLOR.items():
        m = L == k
        rgba[m] = matplotlib.colors.to_rgba(col, alpha=0.5)
    ax.imshow(rgba, origin="lower", interpolation="nearest",
              extent=(x_um[0] - .25, x_um[-1] + .25, y_um[0] - .25, y_um[-1] + .25))
    ax.set_xlim(*XLIM); ax.set_ylim(*YLIM)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_title(title, color=INK, fontsize=11, loc="left")
    ax.set_xlabel("stage x (µm)", color=INK2, fontsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(colors=INK2, labelsize=8)
    for s in ax.spines.values():
        s.set_color("#d8d6cf")
    # 10 µm scale bar
    ax.plot([-12082, -12072], [1260.5, 1260.5], color=INK, lw=2)
    ax.text(-12077, 1262, "10 µm", color=INK, fontsize=8, ha="center")

draw_panel(axes[0], "002", "labels_pre",
           "A  PRE-pickup — video 002 (19:55 UTC) + map-003 regions")
axes[0].set_ylabel("stage y (µm)", color=INK2, fontsize=9)
axes[0].annotate("wedge >3L", xy=(-12073.5, 1292.5), xytext=(-12083, 1302),
                 color=INK, fontsize=8,
                 arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=INK2, lw=0.8))
axes[0].annotate("graphite", xy=(-12068.6, 1265.1), xytext=(-12062, 1260.5),
                 color=INK, fontsize=8,
                 arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=INK2, lw=0.8))

draw_panel(axes[1], "004", "labels_post",
           "B  POST-pickup — video 004 (20:19 UTC) + map-005 regions")
axes[1].annotate("tombstone remnant\n(78% ABC)", xy=(-12040.6, 1278.9),
                 xytext=(-12030, 1300), color=INK, fontsize=8,
                 arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=INK2, lw=0.8))
axes[1].annotate("sheet here was PICKED UP\n~20:10–20:19 UTC\n(mixed ABA/ABC mosaic)",
                 xy=(-12065, 1290), color=INK2, fontsize=8, ha="center")

# ---- panel C: device frame, topology only, explicitly unregistered ----
ax = axes[2]
ax.set_facecolor(SURF)
ax.set_xlim(0, 10); ax.set_ylim(0, 10)
ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
for s in ax.spines.values():
    s.set_color("#d8d6cf"); s.set_linestyle("--")
ax.set_title("C  DEVICE FRAME — NOT REGISTERED to A/B", color=INK,
             fontsize=11, loc="left")

VERDICT = {"sr1": (C_ABA, 1.0, "sr1  B_SD–L4   ABA (strong, two-branch)"),
           "sr3": (C_ABA, 0.45, "sr3  L3–L2      ABA (consistent-with)"),
           "sr2": (GRAY_EDGE, 1.0, "sr2  L4–L1      uninformative")}
# topology-only bar: contacts in device-card order, no geometry implied
bar_x = 3.4
ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((bar_x - 0.55, 1.6), 1.1, 6.6,
                            boxstyle="round,pad=0.1", fc="#eceae4", ec=INK2))
ypos = {"T_SD": 8.0, "L_1": 6.9, "L_2": 5.8, "L_3": 4.7, "L_4": 3.6, "B_SD": 2.0}
for name, yy in ypos.items():
    ax.plot([bar_x - 0.95, bar_x - 0.55], [yy, yy], color=INK2, lw=1.5)
    ax.text(bar_x - 1.1, yy, name, ha="right", va="center", color=INK, fontsize=8)
segs = {"sr1": (ypos["B_SD"], ypos["L_4"]), "sr2": (ypos["L_4"], ypos["L_1"]),
        "sr3": (ypos["L_3"], ypos["L_2"])}
for i, (ch, (y0, y1)) in enumerate(segs.items()):
    col, al, _ = VERDICT[ch]
    xoff = bar_x + 0.8 + 0.55 * i
    ax.plot([xoff, xoff], [y0, y1], color=col, alpha=al, lw=5,
            solid_capstyle="butt")
    ax.text(xoff, (y0 + y1) / 2 + (0.35 if ch == "sr2" else 0), " " + ch,
            color=INK, fontsize=8, va="center")
for i, ch in enumerate(("sr1", "sr3", "sr2")):
    col, al, txt = VERDICT[ch]
    ax.plot(0.6, 0.9 - 0, marker="none")
    ax.plot([0.5, 0.9], [1.15 - 0.38 * i] * 2, color=col, alpha=al, lw=5)
    ax.text(1.05, 1.15 - 0.38 * i, txt, color=INK, fontsize=8, va="center")
ax.text(5.0, 9.35, "No frame bridge in the inputs links this Hall bar to the\n"
        "stage frame of panels A/B — no optical image of the finished\n"
        "device, no GDS, no build-step testimony. Even whether the\n"
        "channel came from the picked-up sheet (A, mixed mosaic) or\n"
        "a later pickup of the remnant (B, ABC-dominant) is undetermined.",
        color=INK2, fontsize=8, ha="center", va="top")
ax.text(5.0, 1.6, "Contact order per device card; segment lengths/positions\n"
        "schematic only (no geometry in inputs).", color=INK2, fontsize=7,
        ha="center", style="italic")

# shared legend
handles = [plt.Rectangle((0, 0), 1, 1, fc=matplotlib.colors.to_rgba(c, 0.6))
           for c in (C_ABC, C_ABA, GRAY_EDGE)]
fig.legend(handles, ["ABC-stacked (Raman)", "ABA-stacked (Raman)",
                     "edge / unassigned / uninformative"],
           loc="lower center", ncol=3, frameon=False, fontsize=9,
           bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.01))
fig.suptitle("vti-01 registration — Raman regions on the stage frame (A, B); "
             "transport channels have no bridge into that frame (C)",
             color=INK, fontsize=12, x=0.05, ha="left")
fig.savefig("registration.png", dpi=170, facecolor=SURF)
print("wrote registration.png")

# ------------------------------------------------------- machine-readable
reg = {
    "frames": {
        "stage": "WITec stage µm (WorldOrigin coords), the common frame of panels A/B",
        "map003": "scan pixels of Scan LA 003 (pre-pickup survey)",
        "map005": "scan pixels of Scan LA 005 (post-pickup)",
        "video002/004/007": "video image pixels",
        "device": "finished vti-01 Hall bar (transport channels sr1/sr2/sr3)",
    },
    "edges": [
        {"from": "map003", "to": "stage", "how": "in-file TDSpaceTransformation",
         "uncertainty_um": 1.0,
         "basis": "003 vs 005 same-region agreement ~1 µm (Raman contract hedge 7)"},
        {"from": "map005", "to": "stage", "how": "in-file TDSpaceTransformation",
         "uncertainty_um": 1.0, "basis": "same"},
        {"from": f"video{t}", "to": "stage", "how": "in-file TDSpaceTransformation",
         "uncertainty_um": 2.0,
         "basis": "map005-on-video004 registration r=0.77, no flip (Raman contract); "
                  "sheet-darker-than-background check reproduced here (f2 stdout)"}
        if False else None,
    ],
    "video_to_stage": {
        tag: {"world_origin_um": V[f"wo{tag}"][:2].tolist(),
              "affine_2x3_px_to_um": world_transform(tag)[:2].tolist(),
              "um_per_px": float(V[f"scale{tag}"][0, 0]),
              "rotation_deg": float(np.degrees(np.arctan2(
                  V[f"rot{tag}"][1, 0], V[f"rot{tag}"][0, 0]))),
              "utc": str(V[f"utc{tag}"])}
        for tag in ("002", "004", "007")
    },
    "region_masks": "inputs/regions.npz (labels_pre/labels_post on x_um/y_um grid, "
                    "0.5 um/px, already in the stage frame)",
    "registration_uncertainty": {
        "raman_internal_um": "1-2 (map<->map and map<->video), vs 5-20 um domain "
                             "scale: domains are resolved within the Raman frame",
        "stage_to_device": "NO BRIDGE - unbounded. No transform exists; no channel "
                           "can be placed on any lamella. Source material of the "
                           "device (picked-up sheet vs remnant) also undetermined."
    },
    "timeline_attachment": {
        "map003_labels_pre": "2026-05-28 19:57 UTC, flake on substrate, PRE-pickup",
        "map005_labels_post": "2026-05-28 20:20 UTC, remnant after ~20:10-20:19 pickup",
        "transport_runs_0_18": "2026-08-18..20, finished encapsulated dual-gated "
                               "device at 1.2-15 K (call, ana cell 33)",
        "transport_runs_19_20": "2026-08-20, same cooldown (addendum, ana cell 38)",
        "gap": "~3 months of unrecorded processing (pickup -> encapsulation -> "
               "gating -> cooldown) between Raman evidence and transport evidence",
    },
}
reg["edges"] = [e for e in reg["edges"] if e]
for t in ("002", "004", "007"):
    reg["edges"].append(
        {"from": f"video{t}", "to": "stage", "how": "in-file TDSpaceTransformation",
         "uncertainty_um": 2.0,
         "basis": "map005-on-video004 registration r=0.77, no flip (Raman "
                  "contract); sheet-darker-than-background check reproduced "
                  "here (f2 stdout)"})
reg["edges"].append(
    {"from": "stage", "to": "device", "how": "NONE — no bridge supplied",
     "uncertainty_um": None,
     "basis": "no optical/GDS of finished device, no build-step testimony"})
with open("registration.json", "w") as fh:
    json.dump(reg, fh, indent=2)
print("wrote registration.json")

# vti-01 — fused Raman × transport stacking verdict (2026-08-24)

Fusion of the locked transport call (`inputs/transport-call.md`, ana cell 33 +
addendum cell 38) with the locked Raman read (`inputs/raman-contract.md`).
Method derived for this step: (1) re-verify each contract's machine-checkable
content from its own raw inputs; (2) build the one coordinate frame the
supplied bridges actually support and state where they run out; (3) fuse per
channel, letting each modality contribute only at the resolution the
registration supports.

**Headline: the two modalities do not disagree anywhere — but they also never
meet on the same patch of crystal.** Transport gives a region-specific ABA
call on sr1; Raman gives a material-level census of the parent flake (mixed
ABA/ABC, ~50:50). The missing stage↔device bridge means Raman cannot be
attached to any named channel, so no fused row is upgraded above its
transport strength; sr2 remains a fused **cannot tell**. One genuine
cross-modality inference does survive: transport's strong ABA on sr1 is
*compatible* with a device built from the picked-up mixed sheet and *in
tension* with a device built from the ABC-dominant remnant — the inputs do
not say which happened.

## 1. Per-channel table

| Channel | Transport verdict (strength; evidence stage) | Raman verdict (strength; build stage it attaches to) | Fused verdict (strength) | Basis for the fused row |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **sr1** (B_SD–L4) | **ABA / Bernal (strong, two-branch)** — BL fraction 0.87·F_L at scale 1.0; m\* = 0.049(2) mₑ vs ABA-BL 0.060 (ABC 0.108 excluded); A/2 = same-mass modulation; ML branch directly resolved (runs 19–20, f_ML = 4.7 ± 0.6 T at n = −1.74); Luttinger closes at λ = 1.14. Finished device, cooldown 2026-08-18→20. | **No region assignable** — no stage↔device bridge. Material level: parent sheet was mixed ABA/ABC ~50:50, lamellar 5–20 µm (strong); remnant 78% ABC (strong). Attaches to build stage: flake-on-substrate, 2026-05-28, pre-encapsulation (map 003 pre-pickup 19:57 UTC; map 005 post-pickup 20:20 UTC). | **ABA / Bernal (strong)** | Carried entirely by transport, which is region-specific and post-processing. Raman contributes no channel-scale test (registration gap) but is materially compatible: ABA lamellae were ~50% of the likely source sheet. Not decisive — transport's own softness (ML mass unmeasured, λ = 1.14 pending QH lever-arm, LK fit unreviewed) is inherited unchanged. |
| **sr2** (L4–L1) | **Uninformative** — weak pair, signals near ADC floor throughout; no frequency content ever resolved. | **No region assignable** (same registration gap). Material level as above. | **Cannot tell** (no strength — no evidence from either side reaches this segment) | Neither modality constrains this crystal. Not a benign gap: if the device is pickup-origin and domains are static, ~50% of source area was ABC, so sr2's segment could plausibly be ABC or mixed and nothing measured would show it. Transport's "no positive ABC evidence on any channel" is absence of signal here, not evidence of absence. |
| **sr3** (L3–L2) | **ABA (consistent-with)** — matches sr1 on all frequency content (fan + spot checks); ML corroborated at lower SNR (run 19); no independent mass, LK amplitudes SNR-limited/non-monotonic. | **No region assignable** (same). Material level as above. | **ABA (moderate)** | Transport concordance with sr1 across the full frequency content plus ML corroboration, on a physically distinct segment, is more than "weak" but lacks an independent mass — so moderate, not strong. Raman adds material compatibility only; it cannot confirm sr3 and sr1 sit on the same lamella (or different ones). |

Device-level synthesis (not a contract row): the fused picture of *the whole
device* is weaker than sr1's row. If vti-01 came from the 20:10–20:19 pickup,
the Hall bar sits somewhere in a ~50:50 ABA/ABC mosaic with 5–20 µm domains;
transport then localizes ABA under sr1 (and probably sr3), while ABC lamellae
elsewhere in the device — under sr2, the gates' singly-gated arms, or the
contacts — are unconstrained and entirely consistent with both contracts.
Transport's hedge "small-area ABC domains below spectral weight cannot be
excluded" and Raman's mosaic are the same statement seen from two sides.
Conversely, a remnant-origin device (78% ABC, ABA only in 66 µm² of
edge-adjacent strips read *weak*) sits in tension with transport's strong,
two-branch ABA on sr1; the fusion therefore *disfavors* remnant origin under
a static-domain assumption, but cannot rule it out because domains are mobile
under processing (hedge H3) and origin was never recorded (hedge H2).

## 2. Registration

**Artifacts: `registration.png` (figure) and `registration.json`
(machine-readable transforms + edge list); regenerated by
`f2_registration.py` from `f1_extract_videos.py` → `fusion_videos.npz`
(videos re-extracted from `vti-01.wip` with an independent parser,
`f0_parse_wip.py`).**

What the supplied bridges support — one frame, the **WITec stage µm frame**:

- **map 003 / map 005 → stage**: in-file `TDSpaceTransformation` per map;
  cross-map residual ~1 µm (Raman contract hedge 7). `inputs/regions.npz`
  already delivers the region labels on this frame (0.5 µm grid); its areas,
  centroids, and remnant ABC fraction reproduce the Raman contract's numbers
  exactly (528 / 516 / 236 / 66 / 66 / 39 µm²; 78% ABC post-pickup; checked
  here, stdout of the check in §archive).
- **videos 002 / 004 / 007 → stage**: in-file transforms (0.04913 µm/px,
  rotation −0.513°, WorldOrigins matching `raman-provenance.md` to the cm⁻²
  digit); verified independently here by a photometric check — region-mask
  sheet pixels sample darker video gray than background in both epochs
  (75.7 vs 102.9 pre; 79.2 vs 99.3 post), i.e. the overlay lands on the
  flake. Uncertainty ≤ 2 µm.
- **Registration uncertainty vs feature scale**: 1–2 µm against 5–20 µm
  lamellae — *within* the Raman frame, domains are comfortably resolved; the
  Raman contract's region calls are spatially sound.
- **stage → device (sr1/sr2/sr3): NO BRIDGE.** The inputs contain no optical
  image of the finished Hall bar, no GDS, no build-step list; the in-file
  videos show only the bare flake before/after pickup, months before
  fabrication was complete. **Correspondence cannot be established for any
  channel.** Cost, per row: Raman is demoted from region-resolved evidence to
  a material-level prior for all three channels; that is why sr1 gains
  nothing, sr3 gains nothing beyond compatibility, and sr2 stays cannot-tell.
  The channel segments' physical lengths are also absent from the inputs, so
  it cannot even be said whether one segment averages over several lamellae
  or sits inside one.

**Timeline registration** (also in `registration.json`):

| Evidence leg | Attaches to |
|---|---|
| Raman map 003 (`labels_pre`) | 2026-05-28 19:57 UTC — parent flake on substrate, **pre-pickup**, pre-encapsulation |
| Raman map 005 (`labels_post`) | 2026-05-28 20:20 UTC — remnant, **post-pickup** (pickup ~20:10–20:19 UTC, in-file video evidence) |
| Transport runs 0–18 → call (cell 33) | 2026-08-18→20 — finished encapsulated dual-gated device, VTI cooldown, 1.2–15 K |
| Transport runs 19–20 → addendum (cell 38) | 2026-08-20 — same cooldown, τ = 300 ms extension |

Between the two legs lie ~3 months of unrecorded processing (encapsulation,
patterning, contacts, any anneals). No supplied document covers that
interval.

## 3. Named hedges

- **H1 — Missing stage↔device bridge** (dominant). No channel can be placed
  on any lamella; every fused row's Raman column is material-level only.
- **H2 — Device material origin undetermined.** Pickup vs remnant vs neither
  is not in the inputs; even the flake↔device link (WITec sample `73474_` =
  vti-01) is owner-group testimony, not in-file (per `raman-provenance.md`).
- **H3 — Domain mobility across the gap.** ABA/ABC walls in trilayers move
  under processing; the Raman census describes 2026-05-28, transport
  describes the cooled device in August. Even a perfect spatial registration
  of the *flake* would not close this.
- **H4 — Raman assignment direction rests on literature signatures recalled
  from memory** (Raman contract hedge 1). If inverted, the mixed-sheet row is
  unchanged (both stackings present ~50:50) but the remnant becomes
  ABA-dominant, which would *reverse* the origin-tension direction in the
  synthesis above (remnant origin would become the concordant reading).
- **H5 — Transport softness inherited**: ML mass unmeasured; λ = 1.14 pending
  the QH lever-arm upgrade; LK fit flagged for expert review (no automated
  fit in corpus); T_e ≈ 8 K; single ~109 MΩ source contact limits sr2/sr3
  SNR.
- **H6 — Channel geometry absent.** Segment lengths vs the 5–20 µm domain
  scale unknown; "short pair" (transport's description of sr2) vs the device
  card's L1…L4 ordering is not reconciled by any input — panel C of the
  figure is topology-only.
- **H7 — Layer count is owner testimony in both modalities** (3L). Both
  contracts note their reads survive a miscount, but the model masses/
  fractions quoted are trilayer-specific.

## 4. What would settle it

- **All rows / H1**: a frame bridge — optical image or GDS of the finished
  vti-01 Hall bar registered to the stamp or stage frame. This alone converts
  Raman to region-resolved evidence per channel (subject to H3).
- **All rows / H3 (most decisive single follow-up)**: a post-encapsulation
  532 nm Raman map of the actual device — 2D lineshape survives hBN
  encapsulation — read against the same lineshape discriminators.
- **H2**: build-step testimony from the owner group: which pickup built
  vti-01, and any anneals between map and cooldown.
- **sr2 row**: any signal at all — rewiring/contact repair to lift the
  109 MΩ ceiling, or the step-6 Streda/Chern complement at 10 T+ (ABA's
  non-dispersing ML N = 0 doublet offsets the QH sequence), which would also
  firm sr1 to decisive.
- **sr3 row**: an independent LK mass on sr3 (second density / electron
  side per the transport contract's list).
- **sr1 row to decisive**: ML mass (low-B-window ladder) or the QH lever-arm
  upgrade closing λ = 1.14.
- **H4**: one reference spectrum from a known-stacking trilayer on the same
  tool (or published 532 nm ABA/ABC lineshapes checked against
  `final_lineshapes.png` in the Raman read's archive).

## Provenance line

Inputs received and used: `inputs/transport-call.md`,

The fused verdict is written: `/data/sharpelab/hera-data/raman-vti-01-fusion-20260824/fusion-verdict.md`.

**The fused result: no disagreement anywhere, but the two modalities never meet on the same patch of crystal — so no row is upgraded, and sr2 is an honest "cannot tell."**

- **sr1 (B_SD–L4): ABA / Bernal, strong** — carried entirely by transport's two-branch evidence (BL fraction + mass + resolved ML pocket). Raman contributes only material-level compatibility: ABA lamellae were ~50% of the likely source sheet.
- **sr3 (L3–L2): ABA, moderate** — transport concordance with sr1 plus ML corroboration, but no independent mass; Raman again adds nothing channel-scale.
- **sr2 (L4–L1): cannot tell** — transport near the noise floor, Raman unplaceable. Not benign: ~50% of the source area was ABC, so an ABC segment here would be invisible to everything measured.

**Why Raman couldn't be region-resolved per channel:** the only frame bridge is the stage-registered video inside `vti-01.wip`. I re-extracted those videos with an independent WIT-tag parser and confirmed the whole Raman side registers to the stage frame at 1–2 µm — well inside the 5–20 µm domain scale — but there is **no bridge from the stage frame to the finished Hall bar** (no optical/GDS of the device, no build-step testimony, and no channel geometry in any input). `registration.png` shows this as three panels: pre-pickup mosaic, post-pickup remnant (78% ABC), and the transport channels as an explicitly unregistered topology-only schematic; `registration.json` carries the transforms and the missing-edge statement.

**One real cross-modality inference survives:** transport's strong ABA on sr1 is compatible with a device built from the picked-up mixed sheet and *in tension* with one built from the ABC-dominant remnant — so the fusion disfavors remnant origin, under the named caveats that domains are mobile across the ~3-month unrecorded processing gap and the Raman ABA/ABC labeling direction rests on literature recalled from memory (if inverted, that tension reverses direction).

Verification done along the way: the ana notebook's call cells match the transport contract verbatim (parsed, not executed); `regions.npz` reproduces every area, centroid, and stacking fraction in the Raman contract (`f3_contract_checks.py`); the video transforms match `raman-provenance.md` exactly, and a photometric check confirms the overlays land on the flake. Top settling items are listed per row — a frame bridge and a post-encapsulation Raman map of the actual device are the two that close hedges H1 and H3.
